NAME: Templated Application
DESCRIPTION: Templated applications are applications for which there is a template configuration that allows very easy integration of an application with maximum security while not impacting operations.

NAME: Application Delivery
DESCRIPTION:
The Application Delivery module is used to deploy an application behind the WAF that is not part of the list of templated applications.

Application delivery focuses on delivery rather than security, where the use cases are deployment of applications in various paths on the same entry domain and SSL termination. The module also allows load balancing towards the back end in order to increase the availability of the application.

NAME: Application with Basic Protection
DESCRIPTION: This module is used to protect an application with the regular protection mechanisms of the Web Application Firewall.

NAME: Application with Additional Protection I
DESCRIPTION: This module is used to protect an application with strong security requirements behind the WAF.

NAME: Application with Additional Protection II
DESCRIPTION: This module is used to protect an application that has maximum-security requirements behind the WAF.

NAME: 1 Additional Stage
DESCRIPTION: This module provides additional hardware in order to separate development and production configurations. An additional stage reduces the likelihood of problems on production environments caused by development tests. It also makes it easier to stage new application releases for development and pre-production, because they are separate from the production environment.

NAME: 1 Additional Stage High Availability
DESCRIPTION: This module adds high availability to the additional stage.

NAME: Login Method: Authentication against MC Passport service
DESCRIPTION: A login application is an application that provides an authentication service for a user or a machine to resources located behind the WAF. It also can handle authorizations and additional functionality such as password resets or it can use self-registration. Authentication is typically done against a user directory to which the WAF has a connection. Typical user directories are the Open Systems Identity service, a Windows Active Directory or another LDAP directory. Custom user directories can mostly be attached to the login application with a connector plu- gin developed as a project.

NAME: Web Single Sign-on: Identity Propagation per Application
DESCRIPTION:
This module is available in combination with a Open Systems Web Single Sign-on service only.
